decision: Disclosed that the wording of the decisions from here on was drafted with a separate research session, and required every number to be reproduced with our own tool before relying on it; that session's figures are a check, not a source.
quote: Before my decisions: I worked through each call in a separate Claude session that researched how transit agencies define lateness and independently re-checked this data (notes in takehome/research/). Every decision below is mine; the wording was drafted with that session and I've reviewed it. Please reproduce every number with our own tool before we rely on it.

decision: Remove only rows that cannot be true, each with a reason code (24 UNPARSEABLE, 18 ARRIVAL_BEFORE_DEPARTURE, 1 DUPLICATE); convert T1-02864 and keep it; never trim extreme rows. The agent then found the duplicate pair differs in runtime (45 vs 40) and widened the duplicate key; I kept that.
quote: Bad rows: remove only rows that cannot be true, each with a reason code: the 24 arrivals stamped "08:60" and the 18 that arrive before the bus left. Convert T1-02864 from +00:00 and keep it; count the T1-03235/T1-03237 pair once. Never trim rows for being extreme, because that would quietly delete R-35's Wednesday, the clearest sign riders were hurt.

decision: Late line: more than 5 min after departure + runtime, early is on time; day late if more than half its trips are late; route LATE at 4+ of 7 days; ties at clock resolution go to NOT LATE. My least-sure call; the tool confirmed R-26 is one trip from flipping. Provenance: the tie rule, the on-time windows and the expectation that R-26 is one trip from flipping came from the research session; I adopted them, and the tool confirmed the R-26 flip.
quote: The line: a trip is late only if it arrives more than 5 minutes after scheduled departure plus scheduled runtime; early counts as on time. That's the standard window (TCQSM 0-5, London +5, Ireland 5:59), and the devices stamp whole minutes, so 5:00 is within clock error. A route-day is late if more than half its valid trips are late; a route is LATE if 4 or more of its 7 days are late. The bonus is all-or-nothing on one depot head, so a tie at the clock's resolution goes to NOT LATE. This line is my least-sure call: I expect R-26 to be one trip from flipping. Confirm that with the tool.

decision: Worst three ranked by share of trips more than 5 min late, p85 tie-break; separate from LATE, so a route can be worst-three and NOT LATE. Overrules the agent's first proposal (median of daily medians) and the naive mean.
quote: Rank the worst three by share of trips more than 5 minutes late, with p85 as tie-break, the same unit as the verdict. Not the mean: one bad day (R-35's Wednesday) shouldn't decide a ranking. The worst three is where ops looks first; LATE is the line with money attached, so a route can be in the worst three without being LATE.

decision: REC-114 not applied to any verdict, despite being a signed-off directive: its 4xx selector matches no trip, and by route it erases R-14's lateness by construction. Shown as a labelled side column; recommend publishing 53 min from next week. The agent had recommended not applying it; I set the reasons, the side column and the condition that would reverse it. Provenance: I adopted the research session's reasons, including that 53 min is roughly R-14's actual average trip.
quote: REC-114: don't use it for any verdict. Its selector is the 4xx series, but vehicle_series here holds only the last two digits and equals the route on every row, so no 4xx trip can be identified. Applied by route it lands on R-14, and 53 minutes is roughly R-14's actual average trip, so it erases R-14's lateness by construction; "line up with what the review already has" is fitting the answer. Measure each trip against the runtime riders were given. Show R-14 under schedule_v2 in a labelled side column so Priya can explain the gap, and recommend publishing 53 minutes from next week. What would change my mind: proof riders were shown the 53-minute timetable from 5 Aug; then apply it from that date only.

decision: R-35's Wednesday: keep all 19 trips, R-35 NOT LATE, flag the day as an incident for refund review and a device check; do not cite the ops log. Provenance: the research session found the ops-log mismatch and I adopted it; this corrected the agent, which had suggested the ops log might explain the day.
quote: R-35 Wednesday: keep all 19 trips. R-35 is NOT LATE (1 bad day of 7). Flag the day as an incident, send its trips to refund review, and ask the device team to check them. Don't cite the ops log: HANDOFF says it's last week's, and it doesn't fit anyway (about 35 min, mornings, a corridor vs about 51 min, all day, one route).

decision: Refund queue: any trip more than 15 min late, whatever the route verdict; the refund owner decides; sized in trips only, no rupee guesses. Later corrected: the CESL 15 min caps an on-time window, not a refund standard; DECISION.md now states 15 as a judgment (3x the late line).
quote: Riders: any trip more than 15 minutes late goes to the refund queue for review, whatever the route verdict; the refund owner decides, not us. The 15 comes from the CESL e-bus contract's cap. Size it in trips from the tool, with no rupee guesses, since we have no fares or loads.

decision: Every rule adjustable for the debrief, plus what_if and a flip-distance column; exactly four tests.
quote: Make these adjustable for the debrief: the late line and whether 5:00 counts as late, whether early arrivals count against a route, the majority rules, time-of-day and day filters, excluded trips with a reason, REC-114 off / by route / by vehicle class, and the ranking metric. Add a what_if tool and a flip-distance column (trips needed to reverse each verdict). Four tests only: exclusions, redaction, a 3-day slice, and a regression on this week's verdicts.
